title: Tenant Network Fingerprint Dashboard and Deployment Safety Thermostat
creator: Diego Mendez
description: Design a compact yet expressive dashboard and safety control for Private/VPC tenants that: (1) creates a persistent 'network fingerprint' baseline for each tenant cluster (topology + typical egress/ingress patterns + latency percentiles), (2) surfaces deviations from the baseline with clear remediation actions, and (3) exposes a deployment 'safety thermostat' control that lets operators tune canary aggressiveness based on network stability, cost exposure, and historical upgrade success. The experience should live in the Private Console cluster view and be accessible during rollouts and upgrade planning flows.
background: Support engineers often open multiple tools (logs, topology explorer, billing) to decide whether it is safe to proceed with a cluster upgrade or capacity change. Existing console views show raw metrics but lack a consolidated, tenant-scoped baseline and an actionable 'safety dial' for rollouts. This leads to conservative rollouts or manual pauses. Building a fingerprint + thermostat will reduce decision friction, shorten canary cycles, and make cost-risk tradeoffs explicit.
user_stories: As a platform engineer, I want a one-glance summary of a tenant's normal network profile so I can detect anomalies before upgrades.
As an SRE responsible for upgrades, I want a safety control that recommends canary size and wait windows based on network stability and recent regressions.
As a customer success manager, I want to see egress cost deviations annotated against network anomalies so I can proactively reach out to tenants that might incur unexpected charges.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard shows a persisted fingerprint for each tenant cluster: topology summary, baseline 50/95/99 latency, median egress/ingress volumetrics (24h/7d), and common peering endpoints.
Deviation band highlights (green/yellow/red) appear for any metric > threshold compared to baseline, with quick actions: 'Run connectivity probe', 'Open ticket', 'Pause rollout'.
Safety thermostat recommends canary percentage and step duration; operators can override and see immediate cost + risk delta estimate.
Prototype flows integrated into the cluster upgrade path (canary configuration step) and the cluster detail header (compact fingerprint chip).
Design includes accessibility states and responsive behavior for narrow consoles and mobile-sized tablets used by on-call engineers.

2025-02-20 - Eng review (Marcus Liu): need signal definitions for 'baseline' and mutation window; recommend 7d rolling baseline plus anomaly guard for recent deploys.

decisions: Use a 7-day rolling baseline for fingerprint metrics (latency, throughput, egress) with 24-hour denoising for bursty tenants.
Thermostat will present three recommended modes: Conservative (default), Balanced, Aggressive. Each mode maps to canary % and step duration; operator overrides are allowed but recorded in audit logs.
Deviation coloring will follow existing console palette (green/yellow/red) to reduce cognitive load.
Simulate rollout preview will estimate additional egress cost (USD) and probability of hitting SLO regressions (low/med/high) based on historical regressions.
tradeoffs: Pros: Consolidates multiple signals into one decision surface, reduces context switching for operators.
Cons: Estimations (cost + regression probability) are heuristics; must avoid overconfidence and surface uncertainty.
Pros: Allowing override speeds operations in emergencies.
Cons: Overrides increase blast radius; mitigate with audit trail and optional second approver for high-impact clusters.
